hyperedges.label: Projects v2 CI sync flow (label to board projection)
Adopt-Pocock durability mechanisms for the unseen v2
Stone git lifecycle: commit to PR to merge to release

nodes.label: project-sync workflow
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the canonical status:* issue label onto the Projects v2 Status single-select so the board is a CI-derived projection and never a hand-edited write surface.

nodes.label: Hardcoded Status option-id map (OPT)
nodes.rationale: Six single-select option ids baked into committed YAML; identified downstream as a latent landmine because re-seeding the Status field mints new ids.

nodes.label: Closed-issue job guard
nodes.rationale: Skips sync for already-closed issues so the close-hook's Released state is not overwritten by a late label event.

nodes.label: clean-status-on-close workflow
nodes.rationale: Released has no issue label, so closing must both strip every status:* label and set the project field — the label-less terminal state made concrete.

nodes.label: Set project status to Released step
nodes.norm_label: set project status to released step

nodes.label: PROJECT_TOKEN secret
nodes.rationale: A user PAT with project write scope is required because GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write user-owned Projects v2; this is the irreducible human provisioning step.

nodes.label: Skill (domain term)
nodes.rationale: Defined as the directory containing SKILL.md, not the installed copy — resolves the flagged ambiguity between source-of-truth dir and installed entry.

nodes.label: Bucket (taxonomy folder)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the mattpocock convention so the repo layout is legible to anyone already running his suite.

nodes.label: Namespace (stone- prefix)
nodes.rationale: The flat, name-keyed Central store means a generic name like commit clobbers another pack's; prefixing the whole pack buys uniformity and provenance at the cost of bare slash shortcuts.

nodes.label: Central store (~/.agents/skills)
nodes.rationale: Flat directory keyed by bare skill name and tracked in .skill-lock.json; the flat keying is precisely why the Namespace exists.

nodes.label: Surface (install-mechanism grouping)
nodes.rationale: Grouped by install mechanism rather than by device, because the Claude Code desktop app and the claude.ai desktop app are different surfaces despite both being 'desktop'.

nodes.label: Bundle (claude.ai zip)
nodes.rationale: claude.ai exposes no install API and no filesystem, so a hand-uploaded zip is the only possible path.

nodes.label: Plugin (Claude Code packaging unit)
nodes.rationale: Kept lexically distinct from Skill because the Plugin is the delivery vehicle, not the capability; Codex/opencode have no Plugin concept at all.

nodes.label: Locked scope: seven stone-* skills
nodes.rationale: Persona/voice skills are deferred to feat/voice-personas as one unit rather than dribbled in, and identity-bearing skills stay in private dotfiles because this repo is public.

nodes.label: npx skills CLI install path
nodes.rationale: Primary path because it is the only one that also covers Codex and opencode, which have no plugin system.

nodes.label: Claude Code plugin marketplace install path
nodes.rationale: GUI-native install for the Claude Code desktop app, where opening a terminal to run npx is friction.
nodes.norm_label: claude code plugin marketplace install path

nodes.label: claude.ai zip upload install path
nodes.rationale: Best-effort for the MVP until bundle compatibility is validated against the current uploader.

nodes.label: SemVer pack versioning anchored in plugin.json
nodes.rationale: One canonical number in plugin.json plus release.sh guards (clean main, new tag, matching CHANGELOG section) so version, tag, and release never drift.
nodes.norm_label: semver pack versioning anchored in plugin.json

nodes.label: scripts/check-latest.sh (consumer freshness check)
nodes.rationale: curl-only so it needs neither gh nor jq; the npx path has no local anchor yet because it copies skill dirs without the pack manifest.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md Agent skills block
nodes.rationale: The three-subsection block (issue tracker, triage labels, domain docs) that points into docs/agents/* — the wrapping-layer surface the Pocock spine requires.

nodes.label: stone-commit multi-ticket Closes detection
nodes.rationale: Detection leads with session-named tickets and #N refs because the canonical branch convention carries no issue token; parent issues holding open sub-issues are dropped so a batch PR cannot auto-close a spec.

nodes.label: stone-merge strips every upstream status lane
nodes.rationale: A ticket can reach staged from any lane — autonomous work often merges straight from ready, and a same-sitting bug never leaves triage.
nodes.norm_label: stone-merge strips every upstream status lane

nodes.label: pocock-board.sh -F to -f GraphQL binding fix
nodes.rationale: gh api -F type-infers its value, so an all-digit option id crossed the wire as an Int and was rejected against a String! variable.

nodes.label: afk-ready renamed to canonical afk flag
nodes.norm_label: afk-ready renamed to canonical afk flag

nodes.label: ADR-0002: distribute via skills CLI with stone- namespace
nodes.rationale: Depend on the third-party skills CLI rather than build an installer because it is Pocock's exact model and costs zero install code; keep plugin.json as the installer manifest; prefix the whole pack for uniformity rather than only the risky names.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002: distribute via skills cli with stone- namespace

nodes.label: Flat name-keyed store collision hazard
nodes.rationale: Because ~/.agents/skills/<name> is keyed by bare leaf name, generic names collide across packs and the second install clobbers the first.

nodes.label: ADR-0003: also publish a Claude Code plugin marketplace
nodes.rationale: Adds a GUI-native path for the Claude Code desktop app without displacing npx as primary; supersedes ADR-0002's plugin-path-out stance on that point only.
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003: also publish a claude code plugin marketplace

nodes.label: Shared plugin.json skills array of direct paths
nodes.rationale: An explicit skills entry pointing at a directory containing SKILL.md replaces the default skills/ scan, so all seven nested-bucket skills load with no double-scan and both ecosystems share one key.
nodes.norm_label: shared plugin.json skills array of direct paths

nodes.label: Single-context domain-doc layout
nodes.rationale: Briefs and ADRs are created lazily by producer skills, so missing files are proceeded past silently rather than flagged.

nodes.label: Use the glossary's vocabulary rule
nodes.rationale: A concept absent from the glossary is a signal: either invented language to reconsider, or a real gap to note for /grill-with-docs.

nodes.label: Flag ADR conflicts rather than silently override
nodes.norm_label: flag adr conflicts rather than silently override

nodes.label: Roadmap / Brief / Issue three-level hierarchy
nodes.rationale: The brief carries the why; each child issue must stand alone so an agent can pick it up without reading back to the brief. PRDs are documents plus a Milestone, never issues.

nodes.label: feature to dev to main branch flow
nodes.rationale: main stays the GitHub default because skills.sh and /plugin marketplace add fetch the default branch — consumers must pull stable releases, not integration.
nodes.norm_label: feature to dev to main branch flow

nodes.label: Release-gated issue auto-close
nodes.rationale: Closes #N fires only on merge to the default branch, so feature-to-dev PRs do not auto-close; issues close in a batch on the dev-to-main release.

nodes.label: Kanban board and status projection
nodes.rationale: status:* labels are canonical and the board's Status single-select is a CI-derived projection — set labels, never the field by hand.

nodes.label: Wayfinding operations (GitHub-native maps and tickets)
nodes.rationale: Maps sit on the board because they are long-running human effort; child tickets stay off because their axis is the map plus dependency edges plus the frontier query.

nodes.label: Canonical role to repo label translation table
nodes.rationale: Skills speak five canonical roles and never learn column names, so a repo's richer vocabulary can diverge freely while the mapping stays lossless.
nodes.norm_label: canonical role to repo label translation table

nodes.label: afk flag orthogonal to status
nodes.rationale: afk-ready was judged misleading during the nitimini build since readiness is already carried by status: ready and the flag only names the executor; renaming in place preserves issue associations and burn-up history.

nodes.label: stone-adopt-pocock skill
nodes.rationale: One manual, context-quiet skill that adopts (installs or upgrades) the Pocock suite on any repo in one invocation; disableModelInvocation so it never auto-fires and bloats an everyday session.

nodes.label: Wrap, never fork
nodes.rationale: Calling setup-matt-pocock-skills rather than reproducing its spine means a future suite version is inherited for free instead of chased through local bash.

nodes.label: Read-only preflight readiness gate
nodes.rationale: Never mutates the machine or credentials so scope and PAT changes stay deliberate and in the user's own shell history; halts with the exact copy-paste fix instead of degrading silently.

nodes.label: Live model-discovered role binding
nodes.rationale: A hardcoded slug table breaks on a single rename, so bindings are discovered in order of authority (release notes, installed SKILL.md text, ask-matt router); ambiguous or vanished binds stop and surface rather than guess.

nodes.label: Idempotent delta-reconcile (install-vs-upgrade dissolves)
nodes.rationale: Greenfield is just the case where the delta is everything, so one path backfills what is missing and clobbers nothing the human authored — no separate migrant/greenfield code paths.

nodes.label: Behavioral smoke (anti-silent-success gate)
nodes.rationale: The genesis breakage was a suite skill silently succeeding on an unwired repo, so proof must be a real issue driven across lanes, not the existence of files.

nodes.label: Local gitignored workbench learning ledger
nodes.rationale: Layout mirrors the auto-memory index-plus-siblings pattern; local-only means full fidelity with no sanitization burden and each downstream install grows its own precedent instead of shipping Matt's.

nodes.label: Workbench feedback loop (capture, feed-forward, precedence, bounding)
nodes.rationale: INDEX doubles as retrieval filter keyed on repo-kind so reading is bounded; frequency is primary with recency as tiebreak; precedent stays advisory so the loop does not rebuild the forbidden slug table in markdown; a suite-version bump ages precedent as a soft weight rather than invalidating it.
nodes.norm_label: workbench feedback loop (capture, feed-forward, precedence, bounding)

nodes.label: Board as early explicit opt-in
nodes.rationale: Label-only is the portable default and a complete config; asking once near preflight front-loads the gh project scope fix instead of surfacing it mid-run.

nodes.label: pocock-board.sh deterministic GraphQL helper
nodes.rationale: The one surviving script, because a wrong freehand mutation can corrupt the board; it wraps the un-deletable Status field overwrite, id capture, and backfill.

nodes.label: Kill list: 2100 lines of bash demolished
nodes.rationale: The prior build re-implemented Pocock's spine, hardcoded the exact slug table the founding brief forbade, classified repos with directory probes, and refused migrant repos — competent 1.0-to-1.1 migration tooling mislabeled as the adopt skill.
nodes.norm_label: kill list: 2100 lines of bash demolished

nodes.label: Trackerless local corpus mode
nodes.rationale: A facts/sources/refs corpus is the artifact, so it gets the domain doc and stamp but no labels, no tracker docs, and no board.

nodes.label: Seam 1 runtime acceptance gate
nodes.rationale: Detection and binding are model judgment now, so they are proven by the adoption outcome rather than golden files — which is why the prior detection goldens are deleted, not ported.

nodes.label: CI workflow templates spec
nodes.rationale: Resolves the unsettled 'or' in the adopt-Pocock wrapper's step 2d by making the two sync workflows literal files the skill copies verbatim instead of prose the model re-authors each run.

nodes.label: Resolve project and field ids at runtime by name
nodes.rationale: The variable part is three ids and a six-entry lane map against ~150 invariant lines — inverting that makes the file byte-identical in every repo, survives Status-field re-seeding, and costs one extra GraphQL call per run.
nodes.norm_label: resolve project and field ids at runtime by name

nodes.label: Fleet divergence: two freehand workflow variants
nodes.rationale: Variant A is better on every row but nothing selected for it; with no template there is no mechanism by which the better variant propagates and no way to tell from a repo which one it got.
nodes.norm_label: fleet divergence: two freehand workflow variants

nodes.label: YAML parse gate before commit
nodes.rationale: An unquoted step name containing 'status: *' parses as a nested mapping; an invalid workflow and a correctly dormant one look identical unless you parse the file, so a model that writes a workflow must not be the only thing asserting it is valid.

nodes.label: Hardcoded option ids invalidated by re-seeding
nodes.rationale: Replacing the Status option set mints new ids, so a re-adoption silently stales every committed id; the same blind-spot class as the repo-project link bug — a data-layer operation that succeeds while the human-visible outcome is wrong.
nodes.norm_label: hardcoded option ids invalidated by re-seeding

nodes.label: MVP dogfood scope
nodes.rationale: Ship a coherent installable pack with a lightweight structural gate rather than waiting on cross-surface polish; the ship gate is structural validation, not behavior perfection.

nodes.label: code-explorer agent (roadmap sketch)
nodes.rationale: The built-in Explore agent inherits the parent model and so runs Opus on an Opus session; a global agent pinned to Sonnet captures the cost win while keeping read-only discipline, with repo-local forks only when conventions or hot-file rules matter.

nodes.label: Executor is a facet of readiness, not a lane
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: Making executor a lane doubles the board — every status forks into agent and human variants and status x executor columns multiply for no gain; as a flag you filter with a label query instead of hunting a column.
nodes.norm_label: executor is a facet of readiness, not a lane

nodes.label: Roles as translation table, not identity
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: Canonical vocabulary and board vocabulary stay independent, so a richer kanban is possible without the skills fighting it.
nodes.norm_label: roles as translation table, not identity

nodes.label: D1 - board is a per-repo prompt, not an auto-decision
nodes.rationale: 'Not an app / no prod deploy' does not imply 'skip the board' — the human chose the board in for glanceable visibility, so the wrapper must ask rather than assume.
nodes.norm_label: d1 - board is a per-repo prompt, not an auto-decision

nodes.label: D2 - needs-info reclassified as an orthogonal facet
nodes.rationale: Waiting on the reporter happens at any status, so folding it into a lane (as nitimini does via blocked) loses the signal; an additive-orthogonal facet enriches the fixed six-status spine losslessly.
nodes.norm_label: d2 - needs-info reclassified as an orthogonal facet

nodes.label: D3 - un-deletable Status field must be overwritten via raw GraphQL
nodes.rationale: deleteProjectV2Field refuses built-in fields and two fields cannot share the name Status, so recreation is a dead end; updateProjectV2Field replaces the whole option set and gh has no CLI verb for it.
nodes.norm_label: d3 - un-deletable status field must be overwritten via raw graphql

nodes.label: D4 - CI Actions ported with per-repo wiring
nodes.rationale: issues-triggered workflows always run the default-branch version, so under feature-to-dev-to-main they are dormant until the first release PR lands them on main — expected, not a bug.
nodes.norm_label: d4 - ci actions ported with per-repo wiring

nodes.label: D5 - seed intent slots, defer area
nodes.rationale: Areas are backward-aggregated — born when a subsystem keeps reappearing — so seeding a taxonomy upfront guesses wrong; slot resolution is detect-then-confirm.
nodes.norm_label: d5 - seed intent slots, defer area

nodes.label: D6 - backfill scope: map on the board, children off
nodes.rationale: A second board for wayfinders was rejected as heavier and re-creating list-invisibility; instead kanban status is the shared spine and a map is just a board item whose type is wayfinder:map.
nodes.norm_label: d6 - backfill scope: map on the board, children off

nodes.label: D7 - tracker agent-doc is a first-class output
nodes.rationale: Without the doc the whole spine stays implicit ('modeled on nitimini') and every future session re-derives it; mutating GitHub state alone is not a finished configuration.
nodes.norm_label: d7 - tracker agent-doc is a first-class output

nodes.label: Labels drive, Project field reflects
nodes.rationale: Status is carried redundantly with a clear authority direction: labels are the write surface, the single-select is a CI-set read surface — the key finding for a portable spec.

nodes.label: Six-status set and kanban progression
nodes.rationale: blocked is a side state that replaces and restores the current state rather than a linear column; Released is label-less and reachable only via auto-close keywords on a default-branch merge.

nodes.label: Eligibility on three orthogonal mechanisms
nodes.rationale: afk-ready label (agent-pickup), native assignee (claimed), and a wayfinder-scoped afk/hitl axis coexist; ready-for-agent versus ready-for-human is a flag on one ready column, never two columns.

nodes.label: The board is a flex point, not the spine
nodes.rationale: Labels fully encode the state machine and the board's only custom field is derived from them, so deleting the board leaves the workflow intact; the portable spine is labels + assignees + native sub-issue/dependency edges.
nodes.norm_label: the board is a flex point, not the spine

nodes.label: Contextual slots: intent and area schemas
nodes.rationale: Port the prefix and role — intent selects the acceptance/review lens, area triggers backward-aggregated milestones — and leave the values to each instance rather than hardcoding nitimini's strings.
nodes.norm_label: contextual slots: intent and area schemas

nodes.label: Half 1 - the config seam breakage
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: The skills upgraded cleanly; what broke was that the canonical role vocabulary was never bound to the repo's actual labels, so wiring lived only in the context window and vanished next session.

nodes.label: Silent seed identity-mapping trap
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: The setup seed defaults to an identity map (needs-triage to needs-triage), which is wrong for a fleet using status:* + afk-ready; accepting seed defaults mis-maps silently across every repo.

nodes.label: Preflight wiring check is a hard requirement
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: /wayfinder ran happily on an un-setup repo and built a real map by improvising, so 'the map built successfully' is not proof of correct wiring.
nodes.norm_label: preflight wiring check is a hard requirement

nodes.label: Reconcile config first, then audit the wrapping layer
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: Audit-only misses the config seam entirely, so setup-matt-pocock-skills must run before any prose/command-map rewrite.
nodes.norm_label: reconcile config first, then audit the wrapping layer

nodes.label: Fixed spine across every surveyed repo
nodes.rationale: The docs/agents trio, the CLAUDE.md Agent skills block, GitHub Issues via gh with briefs in-repo, the five-role triage core, and the wayfinder shape hold regardless of content type or repo count.
nodes.norm_label: fixed spine across every surveyed repo

nodes.label: Code-vs-docs flex axis
nodes.rationale: In docs repos the repo is often not the source of truth (a vault, a contracts/ADR set, a local facts corpus), the status:* kanban must be an opt-in overlay rather than hardcoded, and PRs-as-request-surface defaults to no.

nodes.label: Multi-repo to one shared org board
nodes.rationale: Not a super-repo: a shared project-sync workflow auto-adds issues to one org Project, the built-in Repository field distinguishes items, and per-repo Milestones are dropped in favour of board Epics.
nodes.norm_label: multi-repo to one shared org board

nodes.label: Governance-vs-mechanics repo split
nodes.rationale: Coupling points toward the singular and stable, never toward the multiplying — cross-repo ADRs and contracts centralize while live status stays only on the board.

nodes.label: F1 - shared-board PAT is the weakest link
nodes.rationale: On GitHub Free org secrets do not reach private repos and GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write org Projects v2, so every member repo needs its own manual, expiring PROJECT_TOKEN.
nodes.norm_label: f1 - shared-board pat is the weakest link

nodes.label: Pocock v1.1 skill roster and I/O contracts
nodes.rationale: Every engineering-flow skill is slash-gated via disable-model-invocation so the model will not wander into it mid-flow; only code-review and the three vocabulary callees stay model-invocable.
nodes.norm_label: pocock v1.1 skill roster and i/o contracts

nodes.label: ask-matt flow model (one main flow, two on-ramps)
nodes.rationale: Steps 1-3 stay in one unbroken context window so grilling, spec, and tickets share a line of thinking, bounded by the ~120k smart zone; each implement then starts fresh from its ticket.
nodes.norm_label: ask-matt flow model (one main flow, two on-ramps)

nodes.label: Role taxonomy implied by the suite
nodes.rationale: Roles compose as a DAG, not a menu, and role-binding should bind to the role rather than to GitHub specifically because the tracker is a configured seam.
nodes.norm_label: role taxonomy implied by the suite

nodes.label: v1.0 to v1.1 rename and merge delta
nodes.norm_label: v1.0 to v1.1 rename and merge delta

nodes.label: Upgrading a wrapped suite is a wrapping-layer migration
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: The wrapping layer is standardized across ~a dozen repos, so v1.1 handed over a dozen migrations, not one — a manual reconcile is fine once but fleet scale needs a repeatable per-repo migration.
nodes.norm_label: upgrading a wrapped suite is a wrapping-layer migration

nodes.label: Silent contract changes under unchanged names
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: The part that bit hardest: tdd dropped its refactor stage, grilling gained a confirmation gate and facts/decisions split, wayfinder was reframed as an on-ramp — the old shape runs under the new name unnoticed.
nodes.norm_label: silent contract changes under unchanged names

nodes.label: Product ask: give setup an upgrade mode
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: Extending Matt Pocock's setup skill rather than forking it keeps faith with the map's wrap-not-fork decision — same skill, one new job.
nodes.norm_label: product ask: give setup an upgrade mode

nodes.label: Manual per-repo migration prompt
nodes.author: Matt Stone
nodes.rationale: A working prototype of the wrapper's behavior: run setup first, then audit the wrapping layer, produce a reviewable migration plan before editing, and flag ambiguity rather than changing it.

nodes.label: docs/agents/pocock-stamp.md version stamp
nodes.rationale: Markdown plus YAML frontmatter so a human opens it and gets it while the freshness check still machine-parses; it unifies the version stamp, the freshness fast-path, and the role-binding recipe cache in one artifact.

nodes.label: No content fingerprints - key on version string alone
nodes.rationale: Under-engineer on purpose: an unbumped contract change is rare because Matt bumps versions and writes good release notes, so on any bump the agent re-reads SKILL.md live and judges drift itself rather than storing hashes.
nodes.norm_label: no content fingerprints - key on version string alone

nodes.label: Pocock drift report
nodes.rationale: Grouped by kind of change and written to a file because a migration audit across ~a dozen repos is worth a record; the CONTRACT CHANGED section is populated by live re-read, not a stored hash diff.

nodes.label: skills/deprecated bucket
nodes.rationale: Retired skills are kept for reference but excluded from plugin.json and link-skills.sh so they never ship or get symlinked.

nodes.label: Conventional Commits message format
nodes.rationale: type(scope): summary with max 3 action bullets and a Rationale line reserved for refactors/architectural decisions; scopes are discovered from the repo rather than fixed.

nodes.label: Heredoc, never command substitution
nodes.rationale: git commit -F - and gh pr create --body-file - fed by heredoc; $(cat <<EOF ...) causes shell quoting failures with markdown tables and special characters.

nodes.label: Group changes by logical concern, not by staging
nodes.rationale: Users stage iteratively during development, so current staging is not evidence of intended commit units; group by scope alignment, change type, and ship-together dependency instead.
nodes.norm_label: group changes by logical concern, not by staging

nodes.label: Multi-ticket linked-issue detection
nodes.rationale: The canonical branch convention carries no issue token, so session context and commit-message greps lead over branch-name regex; parents with open sub-issues are filtered out so /to-tickets specs never auto-close.

nodes.label: Knowledge-graph refresh rides the PR
nodes.rationale: graphify update runs at PR-create so the graph becomes permanent at merge rather than via a direct commit to dev/master; env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY keeps the CLI on the Pro/Max plan instead of metered API, and a graph.json union merge-driver prevents parallel-PR conflicts.

nodes.label: Sync-before-push over force-push
nodes.rationale: Team setting: a non-fast-forward rejection means a collaborator advanced the remote; rebase and replay rather than --force, which would clobber their commits.

nodes.label: No Co-Authored-By / AI attribution trailers
nodes.rationale: Explicitly overrides default Claude Code commit instructions; commits stand on their own.

nodes.label: Never stage sensitive files
nodes.rationale: Warn rather than comply when asked to stage .env, credentials, keys, or tokens.

nodes.label: Delegate merge to a sonnet subagent
nodes.rationale: gh pr checks --watch parks the session for 1-10 minutes on procedural bookkeeping that gains nothing from Opus reasoning and burns tokens against a long-lived prompt cache; a sonnet subagent returns one summary instead.
nodes.norm_label: delegate merge to a sonnet subagent

nodes.label: Section 2.0 code-review preflight gate
nodes.rationale: CI-check mode preferred (a check matching code.?review); git history cannot prove a local /code-review ran, so local mode blocks and asks. Subagents surface the gate to the dispatcher and never self-waive.

nodes.label: Empty reviewDecision means unenforced, not approved
nodes.rationale: Private/free-tier repos have no branch protection, so an empty decision is the common case; treat it as 'nothing enforced' and confirm rather than silently self-merging a teammate's PR.
nodes.norm_label: empty reviewdecision means unenforced, not approved

nodes.label: Shape-recognizable conflict resolution (Section 2d)
nodes.rationale: Only set/list-add, import-list, and counter/version-bump collisions are auto-resolvable because their correct merge is structural; logic and semantic conflicts stop and report since the cost of a bad merge exceeds the cost of escalating.

nodes.label: One re-run for unrelated flake, then escalate
nodes.rationale: Distinguish a real failure from a flake by asking whether the failed test touches files this PR changed; never loop on re-runs.
nodes.norm_label: one re-run for unrelated flake, then escalate

nodes.label: status: staged kanban labeling
nodes.rationale: Strip every upstream lane (wip, ready, triage) not just the expected one, because a ticket can reach staged from any of them; autonomous work skips wip and same-sitting bugfixes never leave triage.

nodes.label: Gated production promotion
nodes.rationale: Production deploys are high-stakes shared-system changes, so per safe-action norms they need explicit authorization for this specific action; generic auto-mode or background invocation is not enough. The release branch is detected (main vs master), never hardcoded.

nodes.label: Local branch and worktree cleanup after merge
nodes.rationale: Prevents stale-branch mistakes; --delete-branch fails when an active worktree pins the branch, so recovery is worktree remove -f -f, branch -D, worktree prune.
nodes.norm_label: local branch and worktree cleanup after merge

nodes.label: No graph refresh at merge time
nodes.rationale: Committing a regenerated graph post-merge would be a direct commit to dev/master; the graph is already current in the base branch from each feature PR.
nodes.norm_label: no graph refresh at merge time

nodes.label: stone-promote-settings skill
nodes.rationale: Owns the local-to-shared promotion diff, a niche neither built-in covers; explicitly not update-config (in-place edits, user scope) nor /fewer-permission-prompts (allowlist generation).

nodes.label: Analyze-then-execute two-phase workflow
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 diffs local vs repo settings into local-only / repo-only / duplicate / conflict buckets and stops for review; no file is modified until the user confirms.

nodes.label: Sensitive settings stay local
nodes.rationale: Tokens, credentials, machine-specific absolute paths with usernames, personal MCP configs, and apiKeyHelper scripts are flagged and never auto-promoted into the repo-tracked file.

nodes.label: deny takes precedence over allow across scopes
nodes.rationale: Permission arrays merge across scopes, so duplicates are safe to drop from local; but a repo deny vs local allow is a conflict to flag, not a silent promotion.
nodes.norm_label: deny takes precedence over allow across scopes

nodes.label: skills/in-progress bucket
nodes.rationale: Drafts not yet ready to ship, excluded from plugin.json and link-skills.sh until they promote out.

nodes.label: stone-adopt-pocock skill
nodes.rationale: disableModelInvocation: true — manual, rare, context-quiet; the model never auto-fires it so it cannot bloat everyday sessions.

nodes.label: Wrap, never fork
nodes.rationale: Pocock's setup-matt-pocock-skills owns the suite spine (docs/agents/*, the label set, installed skills); the wrapper authors only the thin Stone delta and trusts his half transitively via the behavioral smoke rather than second-guessing it.

nodes.label: One idempotent delta-reconcile (install == upgrade)
nodes.rationale: No mode detection and no branching on repo age: greenfield is just the case where the delta is everything. Backfill what is missing, clobber nothing human-authored, and a re-run produces zero diff.

nodes.label: Single go/no-go approval checkpoint
nodes.rationale: The directive declares goal, per-repo success criteria, detected slots, and planned mutations once; on go the run proceeds autonomously and re-surfaces only on a true blocker.

nodes.label: Behavioral smoke (anti-silent-success)
nodes.rationale: Proves the wiring runs rather than that files exist: drive a throwaway issue across status:* lanes with gh, verify the board reflects each move, then guarantee cleanup even on mid-smoke failure.

nodes.label: Transient de-GSD nudge
nodes.rationale: A hint, not durable machinery — no classifier table, no stamp field, no regex battery. It fires on GSD residue (phase-N branch law, W<n>-<m> issue titles), never rewrites history or auto-renames live issues, and no-ops once the residue is gone.

nodes.label: Preflight read-only readiness gate
nodes.rationale: Preflight never mutates the machine or credentials — no gh auth refresh, no writes. It prints the exact copy-paste fix so scope/PAT changes stay in Matt's own shell history.

nodes.label: Halt on the first gap
nodes.rationale: One gap emits its fix and stops — no silent degrade, no half-run, no working around it. Checks 1-4 halt; check 5 is the sole advisory.

nodes.label: PROJECT_TOKEN board advisory (non-blocking)
nodes.rationale: Surfaced up front at the gate where the operator expects credential news rather than mid-run in step 4; the CI board-sync workflow just stays dormant until the secret exists and reaches the default branch, so its absence never halts.

nodes.label: Conditional project scope check
nodes.rationale: Label-only is the portable default and needs no project scope, so the scope check applies only under board opt-in and is skipped entirely for trackerless-local adoption.

nodes.label: Canonical role to board-expression translation table
nodes.rationale: Skills speak canonical roles and never learn board column names; per-repo divergence is free as long as the mapping stays lossless. Released is label-less (the closed state).
nodes.norm_label: canonical role to board-expression translation table

nodes.label: afk is canonical, afk-ready is a legacy alias
nodes.rationale: Standing fleet rule: rename in place so issue associations and burn-up history survive, and rewrite the tokens rather than preserving afk-ready as a per-repo expression. The seeding repo nitimini migrated because afk-ready read as misleading.
nodes.norm_label: afk is canonical, afk-ready is a legacy alias

nodes.label: needs-info is an orthogonal facet, not a lane
nodes.rationale: It rides on top of whatever lane an issue is in and never becomes a board column.
nodes.norm_label: needs-info is an orthogonal facet, not a lane

nodes.label: Targeted reference rewrite, never whole-file regeneration
nodes.rationale: Operationalizes 'clobber nothing': replace only v1.0-named/shaped references in Matt's wrapping layer, leaving surrounding narrative and hand edits byte-for-byte, and leave already-current references untouched so a re-run is a no-op.
nodes.norm_label: targeted reference rewrite, never whole-file regeneration

nodes.label: Projects v2 board projection via bundled helper
nodes.rationale: pocock-board.sh (labels / status-field / backfill) is invoked by its absolute path inside the installed skill dir because cwd is the target repo, not this checkout; never freehand GraphQL. CI sync workflows are written regardless of the board answer and stay dormant.
nodes.norm_label: projects v2 board projection via bundled helper

nodes.label: Live role binding (model-discovered)
nodes.rationale: The prior build hardcoded a v1.0→v1.1 slug table that one rename broke, and its 'alternates' were literally the old names — overfit in code. Discovering the bind live from the installed suite makes the next unseen bump cost nothing.

nodes.label: Tracker-touching role set
nodes.rationale: on-ramp, spec, slice-to-tickets, implement, review, setup, wayfinder. The seam is 'touches the tracker', not this exact list: bind extras the suite exposes, and never fabricate a bind for a role it lacks.

nodes.label: Strict binding authority order
nodes.rationale: Release notes/changelog first (the suite's own record of a rename), then installed SKILL.md semantic contract, then the ask-matt router last because it is a runtime query rather than a durable document. The resolving source is recorded as via: in the stamp.

nodes.label: Stop-and-surface on ambiguous or vanished bind
nodes.rationale: A durable bind that a future session trusts must never carry a guess, so a split or empty bind halts the reconcile and surfaces candidates plus the authority sources consulted.
nodes.norm_label: stop-and-surface on ambiguous or vanished bind

nodes.label: Flag forked commit/merge skills, never auto-rewrite
nodes.rationale: Matt's customization is a deliberate human call; rewriting his fork silently would clobber human-authored intent, the one thing the reconcile must never do. Recorded in the stamp's forked: field instead.
nodes.norm_label: flag forked commit/merge skills, never auto-rewrite

nodes.label: pocock-stamp.md durable version stamp
nodes.rationale: A shape reference, not a fill-in-the-blanks form: copy the structure, discover the values. A stamp that hardcodes a slug table is exactly what the pivot forbids.

nodes.label: Drift / completeness contract
nodes.rationale: bindings + unresolved form the drift/completeness contract and suite_version the version contract; together they answer 'current, drifted, or half-adopted?' without re-deriving anything. A non-empty unresolved means the run stopped-and-surfaced and is not done.

nodes.label: tracker-backed vs trackerless-local substrate
nodes.rationale: A trackerless-local corpus carries labels: [], board: none, and the corpus subset (domain doc + stamp, no tracker machinery); the binding recipe still applies when a suite is installed.

nodes.label: Workbench (v2-durability engine)
nodes.rationale: A local growing ledger of proposed / corrected+why / surprised so the next run's proposal starts from accumulated correction rather than from scratch across unseen future suite versions.

nodes.label: Index + siblings layout
nodes.rationale: Mirrors the auto-memory MEMORY.md discipline: INDEX.md stays one scannable line per run and bodies live in <date>-<slug>.md siblings — the index is an index, not a memory.

nodes.label: Read-before-audit selection
nodes.rationale: Relevance order is matching repo_kind, then recency/suite proximity; siblings with non-empty unresolved are pulled in regardless of both filters so an open thread is never silently dropped. Absence of INDEX.md on a first run is not an error.

nodes.label: Append-after write cycle
nodes.rationale: Every run writes a sibling plus one index line and carries unresolved forward; the write happens unconditionally so the corpus keeps feeding the read-before pass.

nodes.label: Gitignored, local-only, no sanitization burden
nodes.rationale: This repo is PUBLIC, so the gitignore is the guarantee that private-repo detail written into a sibling can never be committed; because nothing leaves the machine, siblings record real names and reasons at full fidelity with no sanitization step. Committed templates carry placeholders only.

nodes.label: The model is the loop (no table, no classifier)
nodes.rationale: Turning corrections into a better proposal is model reasoning over prior siblings, not a scored retrieval engine or precedence table; precedent is advisory and the model records when it overrides it. Consistent with the skill's spine, where judgment lives in the model.
nodes.norm_label: the model is the loop (no table, no classifier)

nodes.label: workbench/INDEX.md template
nodes.rationale: Committed copy is a template with placeholder rows only, never the live index, because workbench/ is gitignored.

nodes.label: workbench sibling template
nodes.rationale: Well-formed YAML frontmatter (suite_version, repo_kind, corrections_count, unresolved) is the schema's acceptance bar; corrections_count should match the distinct corrections in the body as a cheap consistency check.

nodes.label: skills/personal bucket
nodes.rationale: Included for dogfooding despite depending on local conventions that are not broadly portable; identity-bearing content stays in the private dotfiles stow package.

nodes.label: Orphan journal branch in a .journal worktree
nodes.rationale: Keeps bookkeeping out of feature branches and mainline history; .journal is gitignored on the working branch and journal entries are never committed to the current branch.
nodes.norm_label: orphan journal branch in a .journal worktree

nodes.label: Non-git context enrichment (transcripts, memory, plans)
nodes.rationale: Git captures only code changes, but vendor picks, region choices, and abandoned approaches happen in conversation and dashboards; without them the journal drifts from reality within months. Commit-less days still get entries when enrichment finds signal.

nodes.label: Canonical-normalization project-slug resolution
nodes.rationale: The ~/.claude/projects slug mapping changed across Claude Code versions (dots once preserved, now replaced), so one repo's history can be split across two slug dirs; normalize both cwd and dir names to all-non-alphanumerics-to-dash and union the matches instead of hand-building a slug.

nodes.label: The 6-month test
nodes.rationale: Include a bullet only if future-you would recognize or care about it in six months; keep vendor migrations, stack reversals, integration points, and dead-ends with reasons, drop debug sessions, typo fixes, and test-count deltas. The journal's value is density, not completeness.

nodes.label: Redaction before any LLM pass
nodes.rationale: Transcripts routinely contain pasted API keys, so known token patterns (re_, sk-, ghp_/ghs_, AIza, xox[bp]-, Bearer, long hex) are stripped before content is summarized.

nodes.label: Upsert with manual-edit preservation
nodes.rationale: Entries are rewritten without an approval step — safe precisely because out-of-band notes and hand edits are read and merged first, and the generated timestamp refreshes so downstream tools detect the update.

nodes.label: Group by author date, not commit date
nodes.rationale: Author date reflects when the work was done, so a Thursday --no-ff merge of Mon-Wed work still attributes commits to Mon/Tue/Wed.
nodes.norm_label: group by author date, not commit date

nodes.label: stone-journal-status skill
nodes.rationale: Read-side counterpart to /stone-journal: tabulates existing entries by date, commits, generated timestamp, and theme extracted from the first heading.

nodes.label: skills/productivity bucket
nodes.rationale: Generic voice/email persona skills are deferred out of MVP scope onto the feat/voice-personas branch.

nodes.label: stone-ai-sniff-test skill
nodes.rationale: Calibrated for the current failure mode — 'sounds like a capable freelancer who's never met the author', generic-but-competent and voice-flat — not the crude delve/tapestry tells that frontier models mostly dropped.

nodes.label: Voice-neutral quality gate
nodes.rationale: Imposes no tone or register so wrapping skills (make-screed, lithos-email) layer their own voice rules on top; a zine post and a consulting email pass the same mechanical checks.

nodes.label: Substitution test
nodes.rationale: Swap the topic — if the sentence still works it says nothing. Targets how models think rather than which words they use, which is why zero banned words can still fail.

nodes.label: Section silhouette / paragraph-count check
nodes.rationale: Models default to 'header + two short paragraphs' repeated; three consecutive sections with the same paragraph count is a grid. Real writing has a ragged silhouette.

nodes.label: Punchline placement and buried lede
nodes.rationale: Models build to the point via chronological buildup; readers bail first. Restructure to start from the best line — hook first, backstory second.

nodes.label: Specificity over abstraction
nodes.rationale: Models hedge into abstraction unless pushed; any sentence describing magnitude without a number, name, or instance should be made concrete.

nodes.label: Lexical tells backstop
nodes.rationale: Em dashes, clause-joining semicolons, banned transitions and filler vocabulary are a final scan, deliberately demoted below the primary checks because a draft with zero banned words can still fail the substitution test.

nodes.label: SOW as primary organizing frame
nodes.rationale: Grouping by business topic rather than date or artifact type; SOW deliverable line items become the section frame plus an out-of-scope section, and a reconciliation section shows progress against contracted scope.

nodes.label: Technical-to-business-value translation
nodes.rationale: Written for an executive who cares about outcomes: 'pre-aggregate optimization' becomes 'load times cut from 15s to 2-3s', jargon is banned outright, and internal tooling/refactors are excluded unless framed as foundation for future capability.

nodes.label: Recommended Next Steps / future opportunities
nodes.rationale: Strategically important because it surfaces follow-on work: roadmap items marked Planned or Future become conversation starters for scope expansion without committing to it.
